Maintaining LHWL documentation and citations

Source: DOCUMENTATION.md

This is a local, manual release workflow. It does not publish to GitHub, deploy a website, submit to CRAN, install dependencies, or start a cloud task. Keep historical manuscript replication bundles and validated release snapshots unchanged. Start each revision in a new versioned source directory.

The canonical package repository is https://github.com/byuzbasi/LHWL. Use that address for package URLs, issue reports, software citations and GitHub installation examples. LHWR remains the method name. The repository is public; CRAN submission remains a separate, explicitly authorized step. Keep private anonymous-review OSF links out of the public package, website and arXiv source files.

Documentation sources

  • vignettes/lorentz-hgwr-introduction.Rmd: the main English guide.
  • vignettes/lhwr-diagnostics-and-tuning.Rmd: LHWR kernel and bandwidth contracts, selection criteria, F1–F3, local inference and Moran/LISA.
  • vignettes/lhwr-graphics.Rmd: manuscript-style LHWR figure recipes and non-overwriting exports; helpers in this guide are not new package APIs.
  • vignettes/lhwpr-lasso.Rmd: the separate Lasso extension tutorial.
  • inst/CITATION: the authoritative bibliographic records.
  • DESCRIPTION: the authoritative package version and package metadata.
  • _pkgdown.yml and pkgdown/extra.css: local navigation and style.
  • tools/update_documentation.R: checks or regenerates the shared bibliography, GitHub citation metadata and the marked README citation section.
  • tools/build_documentation.R: builds local HTML using an explicitly selected installation with a matching source receipt; refuses existing output paths.

The normal R package build creates the installed HTML vignettes. pkgdown uses the same R Markdown sources for its articles. Do not hand-edit generated HTML, vignettes/references.bib, CITATION.cff or the marked README citation block. The site and maintainer tools are excluded from the CRAN source archive; the Rmd files, bibliography and standard vignette outputs are included. Documentation tools are maintainer dependencies, not runtime Imports.

Adding a paper

  1. Verify the actual public record: title, full author list, year, publication status, arXiv identifier/version and DOI when available. A manuscript being prepared or reviewed is not a published article. Do not invent identifiers.
  2. Add a bibentry() in inst/CITATION, with a stable unique key. Keep the software Manual record with key LHWL. Supported record types are Manual, Article, Misc (including preprints), and Book. Every record requires title, author, year and key; use HTTPS URLs and bare DOIs. Public manuscript records should include a resolvable URL or DOI.
  3. Treat LHWR as the primary methodological foundation. Cite the Lasso paper additionally for Lasso functionality. Add later penalty or application papers only to their relevant sections; do not imply that one paper proves all implemented extensions. A new paper does not automatically make all its authors package authors.
  4. Add the corresponding @key reference and a concise explanation in the relevant Rmd section. Replace any now-obsolete pending-publication wording. Once the primary LHWR record is public, describe it explicitly as the primary methods reference in the main guide and citation instructions.
  5. Run the citation generator with --write, inspect its diff, then run --check. It renders all registered citations into the bibliography, README citation block and CFF references without changing package authors. A preprint-to-journal update should normally retain its citation key.
  6. Update NEWS. For an already released CRAN package, increment DESCRIPTION’s version before preparing a new submission. Unpublished candidate revisions may retain their intended version, distinguished by directory and hashes.
  7. Rebuild, inspect and check the exact candidate. GitHub documentation can be updated separately from a CRAN release; an edit on GitHub does not update CRAN’s installed vignettes or citation record. Batch routine documentation changes into appropriate CRAN releases rather than making automatic submissions for every small edit.

The generator verifies structure and synchronization, not the truth of publication metadata or the availability of a URL. That verification remains an explicit editorial gate.

Copyable local workflow for this candidate

These commands use a reviewed local source checkout and the already installed maintainer dependencies (pkgdown, knitr, rmarkdown, yaml) plus Pandoc. Do not install or update dependencies implicitly.

cd /absolute/path/to/LHWL_source
Rscript --vanilla tools/update_documentation.R --write .
Rscript --vanilla tools/update_documentation.R --check .

Run --write only in a new editable candidate after reviewing the citation source. To build the site using an existing verified installation, choose a new output directory each time:

cd /absolute/path/to/LHWL_source
Rscript --vanilla tools/build_documentation.R \
  . \
  /absolute/path/to/LHWL_site_new \
  /absolute/path/to/LHWL_doc_library_new

The site-build command requires a verified installation of the same candidate. It expects LHWL_doc_library_new/LHWL_SOURCE_SIGNATURE.rds, written by local validation only after successful installation of that candidate. It contains named source-content checksums for DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R files and native source and Makevars files. Version equality alone is insufficient because two unpublished candidates may share a version. The release validation also records SHA-256 manifests of source and outputs. Reinstall and create a new receipt after changing executable source or DESCRIPTION; do not bypass a receipt mismatch. On a different machine use its own working R toolchain.

For a new reviewed candidate, installation and receipt creation must refer to that same source directory. The following R code records the receipt only after the explicit local source installation succeeds. Use a new library directory, with a working compiler configuration appropriate to your host:

pkg_src <- normalizePath(".")
doc_lib <- file.path(dirname(pkg_src), "LHWL_doc_library_new")
stopifnot(!dir.exists(doc_lib))
dir.create(doc_lib)
status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), c(
  "CMD", "INSTALL", "--preclean",
  paste0("--library=", shQuote(doc_lib)), shQuote(pkg_src)
))
stopifnot(status == 0L)
paths <- sort(c("DESCRIPTION", "NAMESPACE",
  paste0("R/", list.files(file.path(pkg_src, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$")),
  paste0("src/", list.files(file.path(pkg_src, "src"),
    pattern = "[.](cpp|h)$|^Makevars([.]win)?$"))
))
receipt <- unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(pkg_src, paths)))
names(receipt) <- paths
saveRDS(receipt, file.path(doc_lib, "LHWL_SOURCE_SIGNATURE.rds"))

Run these R commands from the intended new source candidate, never from a frozen historical bundle. Source installation can leave compiled build products in that editable copy; exclude them from distributed source and preserve the final cleaned-source manifest.

The build does not install or deploy the package and disables reference-page example evaluation; the guide examples execute normally. Standard R package checks test the reference examples separately. HTML math may use MathJax’s standard rendering assets; document examples themselves do not fetch data. Local source operation is not a promise of fully offline browser math assets. The pkgdown builder may also request package metadata from CRAN or Bioconductor and standard static web dependencies. Build caches are scoped to documentation_cache next to the output directory. A restricted-network failure is not an example failure; preserve its log and retry the documented build in a new output directory with authorized network access.

Before publication

  • Confirm package/version/citation metadata agree across all outputs.
  • Check every executable guide chunk; label non-executed installation and alternative-protocol snippets honestly. Do not hide errors or warnings.
  • Review table widths, figure captions, equations, links and narrow-screen layout. Use knitr::kable() for vignette tables.
  • Run a source build and R CMD check --as-cran; record host-specific notes, environment workarounds and unperformed checks.
  • Verify hashes and preserve the final source archive and local site.
  • Confirm the public repository and documentation URL before advertising them.
  • Obtain separate authorization for GitHub publication, hosting or CRAN submission. Multi-platform and internet-enabled incoming checks remain release gates; a successful local documentation build does not replace them.

There is no recurring monitor or automatic publication job. New papers enter this workflow when their verified metadata are provided.
